dpa.name_en: Hungarian National Authority for Data Protection and Freedom of Information
dpa.structure: Single-head authority: an autonomous state administration body led by a President appointed by the President of the Republic on the Prime Minister's proposal for nine years (renewable once), assisted by vice-presidents. Dr Attila Péterfalvi was its first President (nominated 2011); the current holder was not confirmed.
dpa.regional: Single national authority, no regional DPAs. It also supervises freedom of information.

law.name: Act CXII of 2011 on the Right of Informational Self-Determination and on Freedom of Information (Infotv.), read with Act CL of 2016 on General Public Administration Procedure (Ákr.) and Act I of 2017 on Administrative Court Procedure (Kp.)

complaint.how: Two routes: a notification (bejelentés) triggering an informal investigation (vizsgálati eljárás), or a request (kérelem) by the data subject for a formal data protection authority procedure (adatvédelmi hatósági eljárás). Filing via the online case portal, government e-delivery (KR ID 429616918) or post (1363 Budapest, Pf. 9); procedures cannot be started by ordinary email. The request must identify the controller, the alleged breach, evidence and the remedy sought. No fee for data subjects.
complaint.contact_controller_first: Not stated as a precondition for the formal authority procedure on NAIH's page. NAIH guidance indicates data subjects should first approach the controller; exact legal effect not confirmed.
complaint.deadlines: NAIH must decide an authority procedure within 150 days (Infotv. s.60/A(1)), excluding time for the applicant to supply missing information and suspension periods. Time limit for complaining not confirmed. If NAIH misses the 150-day deadline it must pay the applicant HUF 10,000.
complaint.complainant_status: In a procedure started on request the data subject is a party (ügyfél) with full rights to make statements, be represented and inspect the file (Ákr. ss.5, 10, 13, 33).

stages: Notification (investigation) or request (authority procedure), or NAIH acts ex officio
Investigation and evidence gathering, with procedural fines for non-cooperation (Ákr. s.77)
Decision (határozat): warning, finding of infringement, orders to delete, rectify or grant access, processing bans, transfer suspension, administrative fine (Infotv. s.61)
Court review in an administrative lawsuit
procedure.decision_maker: NAIH, acting under the authority of its President (single-head authority, not a collegial body).

fines.imposed_by: NAIH itself, by administrative decision (Infotv. s.61(1)).
fines.public_bodies: not confirmed (no specific national cap or exemption identified).
fines.quirks: Infotv. s.75/A steers NAIH towards a warning rather than a fine for first-time infringements, applying proportionality. NAIH publishes its decisions.

appeal.court: No internal administrative appeal. The decision is challenged in an administrative lawsuit (közigazgatási per) before the Budapest-Capital Regional Court (Fővárosi Törvényszék), which has exclusive jurisdiction; the statement of claim is filed electronically with NAIH, which forwards it with the file.
appeal.deadline: 30 days from notification of the decision.
appeal.suspensive: No suspensive effect (Kp. s.39(6)); interim relief can be sought from the court. Disputed data may not be deleted until the deadline expires or the court rules. Court fee HUF 30,000; legal representation mandatory.
appeal.further: Further review (felülvizsgálat) by the Kúria under the Kp. (not confirmed from a primary source for this packet).
appeal.inaction: not confirmed. CJEU C-132/21 (12 January 2023, on a reference from the Fővárosi Törvényszék) held that Art. 77/78 and Art. 79 remedies can be used concurrently and independently.

private.courts: Data subjects can sue the controller under Infotv. s.23 before the regional court (törvényszék) for their domicile or place of residence, at their choice.

cases.title: Digi Távközlési (data breach, test database)
cases.summary: NAIH fined Digi HUF 100 million (about EUR 248,000). On appeal the Fővárosi Törvényszék referred questions to the CJEU, which held (C-77/21, 20 October 2022) that keeping data in a test database can be compatible with the original purpose but not for longer than needed for testing.

cases.title: BE v NAIH (parallel remedies)
cases.summary: CJEU C-132/21 on a Hungarian reference: the administrative remedy against the DPA and the civil remedy against the controller can be pursued in parallel, with courts expected to ensure consistency.

quirks: Two-track system: a lighter, ombudsman-style investigation on notification versus a formal authority procedure on request, where the complainant is a full party.
Single President rather than a board decides; 150-day statutory deadline.
Appeals go directly to the Budapest-Capital Regional Court within 30 days, filed through NAIH, with mandatory legal representation and no automatic suspension.
Warning-first principle for first-time infringements (Infotv. s.75/A).
plain: You can either tip off NAIH, which may look into it informally, or formally ask it to open a case, in which case you become a party and it has 150 days to decide. NAIH can warn, order changes or fine. Anyone who disagrees has 30 days to sue in the Budapest court, using a lawyer, and the decision applies in the meantime unless the court suspends it.
confidence: Medium: procedure, deadlines and court route come from NAIH's own pages and decisions; I could not confirm the limitation period, fines on public bodies, the Infotv. s.23 court level, damages practice, or collective redress.
